package_info.package_manager: proprietary (Electron app with open source dependencies)
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (affected Mac and Windows versions distributed prior to March 30th, 2023)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CX desktop app was compromised via a software supply chain attack, where a third-party dependency or build artifact was tainted with malware. The malicious code was mingled with legitimate, digitally signed code, enabling targeted information theft, particularly against cryptocurrency companies. The attack leveraged trusted update mechanisms to distribute malware to downstream users.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the Electron app is launched or during normal operation)
execution_context.file_location: Electron app binary or a loaded dependency (possibly a DLL or JavaScript file within the app package)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious payload hidden within an 'icon' file or a dependency, loaded at runtime by the Electron app. (Exact code not provided in the report, but described as malware embedded in seemingly benign files such as icons.)
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely JavaScript or compiled binary code, given Electron app context)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The code executes when the app is run, extracting and executing a malicious payload that enables information theft, such as stealing credentials or targeting cryptocurrency-related data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of seemingly benign files (icons) to hide malware is a known obfuscation technique. Loading and executing code from such files at runtime is highly unusual and indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Electron apps do not execute code from icon files or other static assets. Legitimate dependencies should not contain hidden executable payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some applications may load dynamic resources or plugins, but not from files masquerading as icons.
key_indicators: Runtime code execution from unexpected file types

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises a third-party dependency or build artifact used by 3CX (possibly via a tainted open source repository or build server).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the 3CX app build.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is distributed to end users via trusted 3CX update mechanisms and digital signatures.
attack_chain.leads_to: End users install or update to the compromised 3CX app.

attack_chain.action: When the Electron app is launched, the malicious payload (hidden in an icon or similar file) is loaded and executed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware runs on the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: Malware performs targeted information theft, focusing on cryptocurrency companies and other high-value targets.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of code from non-executable resource files (e.g., icons) at runtime
Unexpected network connections initiated by Electron app binaries
Access to sensitive files or environment variables by app components not expected to do so
file_indicators: Icon files or other static assets with embedded executable code
Unexpected or recently modified DLLs or JavaScript files within Electron app package
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs not associated with 3CX
Unusual traffic patterns from Electron app processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Electron app processes for execution of code from non-standard files (such as icons or images). Analyze static assets within app packages for embedded executable content. Track network activity from app binaries for connections to unknown or suspicious domains. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unexpected changes to app dependencies or resource files.
